subject: Renewal: proposed pricing ladder, deferred-credit option, and uplift guardrails
messages:
From: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@scalewave.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions — commit size, uplift cap, and deferred credits

Hi Naomi,

We're kicking off ScaleWave's renewal review and had a couple of asks before our internal procurement sync next week:  

1) Our usage spiked during the POC and has normalized — we'd like to right-size the commit for the 12-month renewal. Would Redwood consider a laddered commit (monthly committed tokens) rather than a single annual bucket?  
2) We'd prefer a lower immediate uplift on our committed spend in exchange for a deferred credit if we miss the commit in Q1 post-renewal. Is that something you've structured before?  
3) Can you share the per-token pricing at the breakpoints you typically offer (e.g., <500M, 500M–2B, >2B tokens) and any uplift limits you enforce at renewal?  

We'd like a concise proposal we can share with procurement. Attached our rolling-30 usage snapshot.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connell
Head of AI Platform, ScaleWave.ai
liam.oconnell@scalewave.ai
attachments: usage-report-march2026.csv (csv)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@scalewave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — commit size, uplift cap, and deferred credits

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (your AE) and Rishi (pricing lead) so we can put together a short, actionable proposal. Short answers up front:

- Laddered monthly commits: yes, we can do monthly committed tiers tied to an annual minimum (helps you align to seasonality).
- Deferred credit: we have a precedent for applying unused commit as credits for the first quarter following renewal, conditioned on a modest initial uplift and a hard cap.
- Per-token breakpoints: I'll include a proposed ladder below once we confirm your preferred cadence and current 30-day baseline.

Liam — can you confirm: a) whether you want monthly or quarterly commit cadence, and b) if procurement needs the proposal in an NDA'd PDF or they can accept a standard amendment?

Marissa — attaching their 30-day usage for context. Can you draft a 1-page ladder with two options (aggressive savings vs conservative uplift) and include a deferred-credit clause? Rishi, please flag any guardrails.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Revenue — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
attachments: usage-report-march2026.csv (csv)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — draft ladder options

Thanks Nai — quick draft options below (first pass). I kept the math simple so we can present two clean choices to ScaleWave:  

Option A — Conservative (lower risk for Redwood)
- Commit: 12-month term, monthly committed tokens = 250M (annualized 3B)
- Per-token price: $0.00120 up to 250M/month; $0.00105 for tokens above up to 750M/month; $0.00095 for >750M/month
- Renewal uplift cap: 25% maximum year-over-year on per-token price (upside only), subject to usage stability
- Deferred credit: Unused committed tokens for Q1 after renewal converted to a dollar credit applied to the next invoice; must be claimed within 60 days of quarter close

Option B — Aggressive (customer-friendly)
- Commit: 12-month term, monthly committed tokens = 200M (annualized 2.4B)
- Per-token price: $0.00105 up to 200M/month; $0.00090 for tokens above up to 600M/month; $0.00080 for >600M/month
- Renewal uplift cap: 15% YOY on per-token price provided average monthly usage in renewal year >= commit
- Deferred credit: Same as A but limited to 50% of first-quarter invoice as credit; credits expire after 6 months

Notes / questions for Rishi:
- Are we comfortable with the deferred-credit cap in Option B (50% of Q1 invoice)?
- Do we want a hard annual true-up (force true-up at end-of-year) or allow carry-forward credits?

I can turn this into a one-page amendment and a simple table for procurement.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — pricing ladder feedback

Marissa — good start. A couple of pricing/ops guardrails from my side:  

1) Deferred-credit mechanics: prefer credits to be dollar credits (not token carry-forward) to avoid accounting mismatch. Credits should be auto-applied to subsequent invoices and expire after 90 days. For Option B, 50% of Q1 invoice as a max credit is acceptable if we require a minimum initial uplift (e.g., 8–10% on the ARR) to justify the flexibility.

2) True-up: require an annual true-up at end-of-term. No indefinite carry-forward; credits can reduce next invoice but must be reconciled on the annual true-up.

3) Usage smoothing (ops): accept monthly variations +/-40% from committed monthly tier without penalty; anything beyond triggers a short-form amendment. This helps customers with seasonality but preserves forecasting.

4) Pricing ladder: prefer continuous per-token breakpoints rather than many micro-slabs. The three-tier approach Marissa used is fine.

If we agree to these guardrails, we can present a final amendment. Also recommend adding a 60-day early-termination prorate clause for large discounts.

Rishi
Head of Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 07:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal (Option A/B) + deferred-credit clause — next steps

Hi Liam / Procurement team — appreciate the quick kickoff. Below is a concise proposal reflecting internal alignment; happy to iterate on the call.

Summary: Choose either Option A (conservative) or Option B (aggressive). Key commercial guardrails are included.

Proposal highlights (pick one option):

Option A — Conservative
- Monthly committed tokens: 250M (3B annual)
- Price banding: $0.00120 / $0.00105 / $0.00095 (three continuous tiers as usage scales)
- Renewal uplift cap: 25% YOY
- Deferred credit: Unused committed tokens in Q1 after renewal converted to dollar credits applied automatically to subsequent invoices; credits expire 60 days after issuance; annual true-up required

Option B — Aggressive
- Monthly committed tokens: 200M (2.4B annual)
- Price banding: $0.00105 / $0.00090 / $0.00080
- Renewal uplift cap: 15% YOY (contingent on usage meeting commit)
- Deferred credit: Up to 50% of Q1 invoice applied as dollar credit; credits expire 90 days after issuance; requires a minimum initial uplift of 8% on the renewal ARR

Operational guardrails (applies to both):
- Monthly smoothing tolerance: +/-40% before triggering amendment
- Annual true-up: reconcile committed vs actual annually
- Early-termination: 60-day prorate on contracts with discounts >20%

Attachments: proposed-amendment-v1.pdf (one-page summary + amendment language), usage-report-march2026.csv (their upload).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which option you prefer (A or B) or request a hybrid.
2) If you approve a draft, we'll send the amendment via DocuSign and schedule a 30-min commercial review to walk through the credit mechanics.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/rdw-2026-3782
DocuSign (preview): https://www.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/example-signature-link

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
